edges.effect_quant: Across 166 non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia patients, liver iron concentration and ferritin were already elevated despite little or no transfusion exposure, supporting caution with empiric iron in this biology.
edges.population: people with thalassemia trait, thalassemia minor, or related non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia when iron deficiency is unproven
edges.mechanism: Thalassemia syndromes can suppress hepcidin and increase intestinal iron absorption even without transfusions. If iron is added empirically to a patient misclassified as having simple iron-deficiency anemia, the extra absorbed iron can accumulate on top of an already overload-prone physiology.
edges.summary: Direct randomized harm trials of iron supplementation in thalassemia minor are sparse, but the precautionary signal is still real: thalassemia-spectrum patients can accumulate iron even without regular transfusions, so routine iron therapy should be avoided unless true iron deficiency is documented. This is best treated as a contraindication-style edge rather than a high-certainty pooled-effect estimate.
edges.caveats: This edge does not mean every person with thalassemia trait must never receive iron; documented coexisting iron deficiency can still justify treatment. The risk signal applies to empiric or prolonged supplementation in patients with thalassemia-spectrum anemia when iron deficiency has not been proven biochemically.
